inheritance_basis: The only change between the tested commit and the status postimage is GC_FIXED_INTERFACE_G15_STATUS.json metadata; runtime, bridge, test and workflow sources are unchanged.

first_execution.repair: Commit baseline and observed paths were isolated into fresh subprocesses; runtime, numerical thresholds, ledger semantics and coupling policy were unchanged.

summary.qualification_reference_oracle_note: These are deliberately separate G14 research-oracle runs used only to compare observations. They are not part of the G15 accessor path or its production-facing cost claim.

bounded_conclusions: The FMR groundwater-SWAP participant can expose participant status, q and execution diagnostics from the exact already-executed physical trial through a read-only participant-owned observation snapshot.
Observation reads do not change candidate liveness, accepted revision/time, ledger authority, discard semantics or commit semantics.
A status-6 whole-window failure leaves a diagnostic observation with q unavailable, discards any backend candidate, and does not leak candidate-busy state into the next admissible trial.
Across all 62 frozen FGC44 G14 streaming heads, G15 participant observations match G14 participant status, q and execution diagnostics; max q difference is zero.
The production-facing G15 accessor adds zero backend runs. The qualification test additionally performs one independent G14 research-oracle run per head solely for equivalence checking.

This qualifies only the FMR-specific read-only same-trial observation API as a production-facing building block. E3, P4, tangent-service orchestration and production HCOF/RHS policy remain unadmitted.
